content.overview: Section 41 allows a company to issue depository receipts in any foreign country, subject to such conditions and in such manner as may be prescribed, after passing a special resolution in its general meeting.
content.glance: Special resolution; issue of depository receipts abroad in the prescribed manner and conditions.
content.study: A company may, after passing a special resolution in its general meeting, issue depository receipts in any foreign country in such manner, and subject to such conditions, as may be prescribed. Section 41 is the Companies Act gateway for GDRs; detailed conditions sit in the prescribed rules and applicable frameworks.

sections.heading: Special resolution
sections.body: Company must pass a special resolution in general meeting before issuing depository receipts.

sections.heading: Foreign issue
sections.body: Depository receipts may be issued in any foreign country.

sections.heading: Prescribed conditions
sections.body: Manner and conditions are as prescribed under the Act and rules.

examples.title: GDR after special resolution
examples.body: A company passes a special resolution and issues GDRs in a foreign market under the prescribed conditions.

misconceptions.correction: Section 41 requires a special resolution in general meeting.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should Section 41 be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm special resolution. II. Identify foreign depository-receipt issue. III. Apply prescribed conditions. IV. Conclude.
